title: Next due counts from the Work done date chosen in the step, not the invoice
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to the Maintenance Reminders QA build as an Owner/Admin (any user who can open Settings > Maintenance and create and edit work orders and customers).
  2. Open Settings > Maintenance. Open the schedule 'ZZAUTOTEST Highway Tractor PM', or create it with New schedule: add service 'PM-A' with a Calendar trigger of Every 6 months and canned lines, for example 'Engine oil and filter change' 0.8 hours, 'Chassis lubrication, 12 points' 0.5 hours, 'Air filter inspection' 0.3 hours and 'Brake adjustment check' 1.2 hours (4 lines, 2.8 hours). Save.
  3. Open Customers, open customer 'ZZAUTOTEST Fleet Co' (create it if missing), open its Assets tab and open unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 402' (create it with New Asset if missing). Open the asset's Maintenance tab. If the unit is not on the schedule, press Enroll in Schedule, choose 'ZZAUTOTEST Highway Tractor PM', enter a last service date for PM-A about seven months ago (for example 6 Mar 2026) and press Enroll. PM-A now reads Overdue on the Maintenance tab.
  4. On the customer page press New Work Order, choose unit 'ZZAUTOTEST 402' and create the work order (it opens as an estimate). Note its number, for example S3780-15904.
  5. On the work order page, find the Maintenance schedule card inside the asset card at the top and press Expand.
  6. On the PM-A row press Add Service; in the Add PM-A to <work order number> window keep Add to this work order selected and press Add. The row now reads Added · 4 lines.
  7. On the Lines tab complete every PM-A line today.
custom_steps:
1. Open the Finance tab and press Create Invoice.
  2. In When was the maintenance done? change PM-A's Work done date to 14 Sep 2026 and read the next due shown for it.
  3. Change the date again to 1 Aug 2026 and read the next due again.
  4. Press Confirm dates and record the payment. Open the asset's Maintenance tab and read PM-A.
  5. When the step opens, read the line beneath its title and the column headings.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • The proposed date can be edited and names the day the work was done.
  • With 14 Sep 2026 the next due follows PM-A's interval of 6 months: Mar 2027; changed to 1 Aug 2026 it updates at once to Feb 2027 (if the step shows no next due, check it on the Maintenance tab after confirming).
  • After confirming, PM-A counts from 1 Aug 2026, not from the invoice date (today): its next due is Feb 2027.
  • Beneath the title the step explains the date (in the design: “The next reminder counts from the date the work was done, not the invoice date. Change a date if the work was finished earlier.”), with the column Work done.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10574 (S18, Complete a service and reset the cycle); Chunk 2 MR (Confluence 897679389) as edited 5 October 2026, S18; Design MR_V2_2 (Claude Design export, 6 Oct 2026), driven in full on 6 Oct 2026, Chunk 2 board artboards I1–I6; read 6 Oct 2026. Source-verified 6 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S18-R14: “The proposed date is editable and names the day the work was done. The next due follows from it through the service's own interval and updates as it changes, so a shop invoicing weeks late resets from the work rather than from the paperwork”
  • Design, Chunk 2 board, artboards I1–I6, line beneath the step title: “The next reminder counts from the date the work was done, not the invoice date. Change a date if the work was finished earlier.”
